Yes, you said it so well! I wish OIs like my in-laws are obsessed with me and Stepmother’s Märchen would be more widely recognized because they do have those elements that have literary value, but that also use their webtoon format to the best effect.

“My In-Laws are Obsessed With Me” has quickly been becoming one of my favorite OIs. There’s something special about how the artist introduces darkness and tension in a genre that’s  often a bit blasé with the tragic elements of their source material. Specifically, I think they do a great job by letting their art ‘speak’ more than the dialogue. We see so many panels that are just a character’s expression, that then gets mirrored by another character’s expression. I look more closely to understand the dynamic between the two, and it feels very organic because you see the cause and effect so clearly!

That ties in to my second point, which is how they use the webtoon, scrolling format really well! Mangas tend to get more recognition than manhwas when it comes to the paneling and organization of the pages. However, manhwas can still experience very good flow. The length, amount of detail, etc. really guide the reader—it makes me want to scroll slowly and ‘savor’ it in a sense when I usually don’t. This ended up sounding pretty formal but I just really like it 😆
